survivors.claim: The disposer-return ref-pool guard was loosened from exact array membership (`poolRefs.includes(ref)`) to substring match (`poolRefs.some((p) => ref.includes(p))`) in commit c535407 (titled 'tighten'). Any ref that merely contains a pool ref (`s01`, `s0x`, `s10` against `s1`, `leg:reconcile-extra`) now passes D8's 'matches nothing' refusal; the mark is only stopped one step later by verdict.js's contradiction guard, with the wrong error text and after `disposer-return-<n>.json` has already been written to the sidecar — the orphan write AC-20260909-04-9 says must never happen.
survivors.impact: A stale or mistyped disposition reference that happens to contain a real one is no longer refused by name; the session sees a misleading count-overflow error instead, and a refused mark leaves a copy of the bad return behind in the review sidecar.
survivors.evidence: Spec Contracts: `an entry whose ref is not in the hard pool → exit 2 "matches nothing in the survivor or leg-finding pools"`; AC-20260909-04-9: `...exit 2 with stderr containing "matches nothing in the survivor or leg-finding pools" and write no disposer-return-1.json`. Hunk (c535407): `-      if (!poolRefs.includes(ref)) {` / `+      if (!poolRefs.some((p) => ref.includes(p))) {`. Executed repro (real driver via tests/review/disposer-gate.fixtures makeHost; return [hard s0, soft], disposer entries {s0 waive},{s01 waive}): STATUS 2 · STDERR `spec-review-driver: verdict.js: waived 2 > hard pool 1 (...) — dispositions cannot exceed what was actually found across both pools` · MATCHES_NOTHING false · ORPHAN_FILE_WRITTEN true (disposer-return-1.json exists in the sidecar) · STATE DISPOSITIONS. The pre-image `poolRefs.includes(ref)` refuses `s01` at the D8 site before any write. No disposer ref shape in tests/ or spec/agents/disposer.md carries a suffix that would need substring matching (grep over `ref:` in tests/review and disposer.md finds only `s<i>` / `leg:<name>`).

survivors.claim: D10's dispositions-time cap refusal is implemented as `marks.escalated && tally.fix > 0` (in-session trip only), narrower than the locked Contract line `cap spent (see handleFixApplied's count) and any effective 'fix' → exit 2`, which names the manifest-count + uncleared-escalate-row arithmetic. The deviations sidecar documents why (two hardened pins — AC-20260820-07-8/AC-13 and escalate-cap-durable — force the wider form to opposite outcomes), but the spec's Contracts block still states the wider form.
survivors.impact: The spec's written contract and the shipped behavior disagree on when a fix recommendation is refused at a spent cap; a later reader trusting the spec text will expect a refusal that only the following fix-applied step actually produces.
survivors.evidence: Spec Contracts line 96: `cap spent (see handleFixApplied's count) and any effective 'fix' → exit 2 naming "iteration cap 2"`. Code: `if (marks.escalated && tally.fix > 0) { die('iteration cap 2 reached — ...') }` with an in-code comment stating the durable half is 'deliberately NOT mirrored here'. Deviations sidecar entry 'Fix-worker pass (post-review disposition fix, finding at spec-review-driver.js ~line 1328)' records the rationale. AC-20260909-04-10's test passes on the narrower condition (escalate-row-step.test.js drives marks.escalated via a refused third fix-applied). Advisory: amend the Contract line at close so text and mechanism match.
